Brand, 51, showed no emotion as judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with "staggering arrogance" and shown "contempt" for his victims, who had suffered significant and lasting harm. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.

items.title: Will Eisenkot succeed in 'minefield of Israeli politics' where 'so many other generals' have failed?
items.desc: François Picard welcomes Dahlia Scheindlin, Israeli author, political analyst, strategic consultant and pollster, to examine a question that reaches far beyond the immediate struggle for power: Can Israel move beyond Netanyahu amid coalition deadlock, growing disillusionment in Washington and the persistent limits of political inclusion? As Gadi Eisenkot embarks on a 45-day race to form a government, following Israeli President Isaac Herzog's decision to entrust him with the task of assembling an elusive parliamentary majority, Scheindlin offers a timely reminder: “It's always too early to eulogize Netanyahu politically.” seemingly insurmountable political crises.

items.title: Republican congressman launches impeachment bid against Pentagon chief Hegseth
items.desc: Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie moved on Monday to force a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, putting pressure on his fellow Republicans to decide whether to remove one of the Trump administration’s most prominent figures following the party's crushing defeat in midterm elections.

items.title: 'We think' the Iranians and Americans want to negotiate, Egyptian FM says
items.desc: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said he believed Iran and the United States wanted to negotiate, but called for a "concrete deal" to prevent another escalation. He also said Cairo was still "counting" on US President Donald Trump to "move forward" with the stalled Gaza peace plan and was "confident" US military aid to Egypt would continue.

items.title: France opens probe into Iranian cyber unit over fridge attacks
items.desc: France on Monday said Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind "unprecedented" cyberattacks on supermarket fridges in the country last month, vowing sanctions on a European level against Tehran. Swathes of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators, in some cases forcing them to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.

items.title: Broken system? French protesters rage against austerity
items.desc: How can the nation of haute couture and high speed rail have an affordability issue? On paper, France boasts the planet’s seventh largest economy. Its top diplomat started the week hosting a Group of Seven Industrialized Nations foreign ministers meeting inside the regal setting of its landmark Left Bank ministry.

items.title: 'Life in Gaza simply miserable': Amid flooding, lack of aid, conditions 'worsen' for Palestinians
items.desc: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Shaina Low, Communication Adviser for the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC). Thirteen months into what she describes as a "so-called ceasefire," the humanitarian crisis in Gaza continues to deepen, exposing the profound gap between diplomatic commitments and the lived realities of Palestinian civilians. In an interview with France 24, Shayna Low, communications adviser in Palestine for the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), describes a population confronting winter flooding, repeated displacement, deteriorating shelter conditions and persistent restrictions on humanitarian assistance. "Life in Gaza is simply miserable." Low urges Israel to "open all the crossings, lift the restrictions, let aid in."

items.title: Social unrest ahead of French elections:  Protesters 'don't believe politics can achieve anything'
items.desc: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University. France's 1.6% minimum-wage increase, in response to the countrywide protests, may offer a temporary reprieve from social unrest, but it does little to resolve the deeper political and institutional crisis confronting the country. According to Foucart, the central problem extends beyond declining purchasing power, fiscal constraints and the limitations of a minority government. It concerns a growing loss of faith in politics itself. “They are in the street because they don't believe politics can achieve anything,” Foucart argues, suggesting that the persistence of mass demonstrations ahead of the presidential election reflects profound disillusionment with the political system's capacity to deliver meaningful change.

items.title: French PM brings forward hike in minimum wage to calm protesters
items.desc: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said ​on Monday, November 9, he was bringing forward a planned hike in the minimum wage to December from January, as he sought to defuse a cost-of-living crisis that has sparked some of France's worst civil unrest in years. Unions swiftly dismissed the offer as "crumbs".

items.desc: Shares of artificial intelligence leader Nvidia tumbled early Monday after the chip company said it launched an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang following reports he was targeted by Chinese intelligence. Nvidia shares were down more than eight percent in opening trading after its board announced that a committee of independent directors assisted by outside counsel would undertake the probe.

items.title: COP31 climate summit: Can we electrify the world?
items.desc: The UN's annual climate change summit, known as COP31, opens this Monday in Turkey amid deep concern following deadly heatwaves in Europe and deadly floods in Nepal. items.title: 针对记者的滥用诉讼增多，法律保护亟待加强

items.title: 来自北极冰海深处的呼声：世界应当相信科学
items.desc: 在漫长的极夜中，一支科考队正随海冰缓缓漂流，记录北极正在发生的深刻变化。海冰逐渐消融，油轮驶入北极航道。这片遥远的冰海正经历着海冰消融与航运活动增加的双重变化，而其影响远不止于北极。在一场跨越千里的视频对话中，北极科考队与联合国秘书长共同探讨了这些变化背后的全球气候挑战，以及为什么在气候危机日益严峻的今天，相信科学尤为重要。

items.title: 难民署：近9000万被迫流离失所者面临严重气候风险

items.title: “教育不能等待”基金6亿美元筹资目标近在咫尺

items.title: 燃油价格上涨冲击全球  发展中经济体负担最重

items.title: 【专题报道 】驶向电气化未来：交通转型如何助力全球气候目标

items.title: COP31前瞻：今年联合国气候变化大会有哪些重要议题？

items.title: 全球升温恐将突破1.5℃温控红线
